items.originalSummary: Fed chair Kevin Warsh isn't committing to another rate hike this month, and traders are increasingly betting he'll wait — despite inflation data showing price pressures reaching more of the economy.The odds of an October hike are falling to roughly 15%, according to Bloomberg's bond futures pricing, down from 33% after Wednesday's hot consumer price report and 24% before its release.That retreat began before Warsh spoke at the IMF gathering in Bangkok, where he declined to preview the Fed's next decision. "I don't prejudge meetings," he said.Treasury yields are retreating too. The 10-year yield (^TNX) is hovering near 5.07%, roughly 29 basis points below its October 7 intraday high. The 30-year yield (^TYX) is near 5.42%, down roughly 32 basis points from its peak that same day. Both are edging lower again today.The inflation details are less reassuring. Bank of America calculates that 55% of the core consumer price basket is experiencing three-month annualized increases above 2.5%. Its economists still expect an October hike.That connects to a concern Warsh raised at Jackson Hole in August: how widespread price increases remain. His analysis examined a different inflation measure, personal consumption expenditures, but similarly looked beyond the headline number to gauge underlying pressures.Traders aren't abandoning further tightening. Futures still price roughly one quarter-point hike by December. Watch whether inflation pressures keep broadening when the government releases its PCE inflation report on October 29 following the next Fed decision the day before.

Meanwhile, Nasdaq-100 futures declined 0.23% as investors assessed corporate earnings expectations and rising energy costs.Wall Street entered the week after gains across all three major indexes. The Dow and S&P 500 recorded their second positive week in three weeks, while the Nasdaq Composite extended its winning streak to four weeks. Technology stocks supported the advance, despite concerns about higher borrowing costs and expensive stock valuations.The current US stock market bull run also reached its fourth anniversary on Monday. However, gains have remained concentrated among large technology companies. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate crude traded near USD 92.65 per barrel, gaining approximately 0.9% during early trading.The recovery followed deadly attacks on Riyadh's international airport over the weekend. President Donald Trump also said Washington was considering joining Saudi Arabia in military action against Yemen's Houthis. However, no final decision had been announced, leaving traders uncertain about further developments in the region.Separately, Trump announced what he described as an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine. He said both countries had agreed to stop targeting each other's energy facilities. items.originalSummary: Dow Jones| Nasdaq | US Stock Market Today | Live: Trump increased investments in drugmakers that benefited from Medicare exemptions, Democrats sayInvestments in pharmaceutical companies made on behalf of President Donald Trump increased significantly after he returned to the White House last year, with his portfolio adding millions of dollars in stock in firms that benefited from a Republican-backed law that shields certain medications from Medicare price negotiations, according to a report from congressional Democrats. The report, released Friday by the Joint Economic Committee’s minority arm, found that Trump’s pharmaceutical stock holdings grew from a maximum reported value of $1.7 million in 2024 to as much as $56.2 million at the end of 2025. The report said that included up to $39.1 million worth of stock held in companies that benefited from exemptions to Medicare’s drug price negotiation program, which came through a provision in Republicans' 2025 tax and spending law. Additional analysis of Trump's financial disclosures provided by committee Democrats showed that his investment portfolio bought as much as $2.55 million in shares of pharmaceutical companies benefiting from the exemptions on three dates before he signed the legislation in July 2025. That included up to $950,000 in purchases on July 1, 2025, the day the Senate passed the bill. His portfolio also bought as much as $1 million in AbbVie stock in August 2025, after the bill became law.

items.originalTitle: Dow Jones, Nasdaq 100, S&P 500 Outlook: Top Catalysts to Move US Stocks This Week
items.originalSummary: The US stock market witnessed a strong buying trend overnight, especially in the Dow Jones, which skyrocketed by nearly 629 points before correcting mildly. On Friday, in the early hours, US stock futures have gained momentum as focus shifted towards the outlook for artificial intelligence and related tech companies. Also, the Dow Jones and S P 500 are on path to record 1% weekly gains, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq is expected to outperform with 2% weekly gains. However, Fridays performance will make it or break this weeks performance.Dow Jones + S P 500 + Nasdaq CompositeOvernight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average or DJIA index skyrocketed by 629 points to hit an intraday high of 52,250.18 before correcting to end at 52,177.69, up by 556.21 points or 1.08%. While the S P 500 index gained by 20.16 points to end at 26,713.02. Also, the S P 500 index surged 25.12 points or 0.33% to end at 7,744.06.The gains came as selling pressure on chip stocks eased after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended the financial position of AI computing provider CoreWeave Inc. Companies such as CoreWeave have taken on substantial debt with backing from suppliers, including Nvidia, raising concerns that circular financing arrangements could be generating artificial demand. Meanwhile, Anthropic reportedly told investors that its third-quarter revenue stood at $16.8 billion. For the week, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite was on track to fall more than 2%, while the S P 500 was down nearly 1%. The Dow was poised to post a weekly gain of around 1%, as per Trading Economics.US Stock Market Outlook For Friday, October 16, 2026:In the early trade, the Dow Jones futures gained by 35 points to trade around 52,465 after the rally in the index on Wall Street. However, Nasdaq 100 futures dropped by 60 points to 30,084, while S P 500 futures slipped mildly to trade around 7,788.50.As per Daniel Munday, Principal Analyst, VT Markets, hotter US CPI revived Fed hike bets, then cautious Fed comments pulled them back. At the same time, AI financing worries hit US tech, with CoreWeave and Oracle sold off on debt fears. Asia took the hit, and the KOSPI closed down 7.57%, its seventh straight loss, with foreign investors heavy sellers.Overnight, he added, the US yields and the dollar eased as a Bloomberg report suggested China holds more US debt than official data show, and as investors sought safety. That helps, and bounces are possible after such a fast fall, but chip heavy markets such as Korea, Taiwan and Japan stay exposed, so volatility is likely until AI and rate worries settle.Key risks are the October 28 Fed meeting, more hot inflation data, oil and Middle East tensions, and whether AI spending can be funded, Munday said.Global market cues remain mixed amid concerns over elevated US inflation, interest-rate expectations and volatility in AI-linked stocks, while investors continue to assess overnight Wall Street performance and trends across Asian markets, said Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking.Investors will focus on New York Fed Services Business Activity, Import Price Index, Export Price Index, Industrial Production, Manufacturing Production, Capacity Util

historyItems.originalSummary: Ford makes the long haul and enters Grasso’s Garage with an aesthetically pleasing and proven F-150 Lobo edition pickup truck that is ready for all consumers. With a 600-mile range on a full tank, our F-150 Lobo tester offers an upgraded 5.0-liter Coyote V-8 engine packed with 400 horsepower and 410 lb.-ft. of torque. Paired with a 10-speed automatic transmission, the F-150 Lobo gets up and goes and is smooth. Wrapped in Oxford White, the Lobo package is an additional $4,695 and includes 22-inch gloss black wheels, an electronic locking rear axle and all-season tires. Our STX Series pickup comes with LED fog lights, black cloth interior and a black and dark gray grill. Upgraded options include a tray style floor liner, mobile office package, 36-gallon fuel tank, SiriusXM and spray-in bedliner for a combined additional $2,630 total. While the interior is simple and typical Ford, it serves the consumers well with its 12-inch SYNC4 infotainment system. Rear-view camera and parking sensors, selectable drive modes and a host of safety features came standard on our weeklong tester. Standard warranty is a 3-year / 36,000 mile bumper to bumper, a 5-year / 60,000 mile powertrain, and a 5-year / 60,000 mile roadside assistance.

historyItems.title: Arista Networks (ANET) 2026 年股票預測與價格目標
historyItems.summary: Arista Networks (ANET) has put high-density AI infrastructure at the center of its story with a new open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio, aiming to link accelerators across liquid-cooled racks for large-scale workloads. The latest AI rack-scale launch lands after a strong run in Arista Networks' shares, with the stock up 15.51% on a 90-day share price return and 57.84% year to date, while long-term total shareholder return over five years is about 8x. At a last close of US$210.88, the 1-day share price return fell 2.70% even as the 30-day gain of 5.66% and 1-year total shareholder return of 43.02% indicate ongoing momentum, supported by prior interest in Arista's 800G switching products and growing attention on AI infrastructure demand.

historyItems.originalTitle: Chip-Machine Supplier ASML Boosts Guidance for Third Time on Surging AI Demand
historyItems.originalSummary: By Mauro Orru ASML Holding improved its annual forecasts for the third time this year and said it was looking at ways to boost production of its semiconductor-making machines even more as the race to build artificial-intelligence infrastructure fuels demand for advanced chips. The Dutch group is projecting annual sales between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros, equivalent to a range of $49.27 billion to $50.39 billion, compared with prior guidance of 43 billion euros to 45 billion euros. Meanwhile, its gross margin--a closely watched metric of pricing power and profitability--should come in at roughly 56%, compared with a previous guidance range of 54% to 56%. The revisions show how much ASML's fortunes have come to benefit from the build-out of data centers that turned chips into a red-hot commodity. Surging semiconductor demand means that ASML's clients like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Samsung Electronics and Intel will need more of its machines so they can produce enough chips. ASML shares in Amsterdam gained more than 2% in European morning trading, consolidating ASML's lead as Europe's most valuable listed company. Its stock is up more than 80% over the past 12 months on a wave of investor fervor around AI and expectations that chips and semiconductor-making tools will remain in high demand for years to come. "Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments. In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030," ASML Chief Executive Christophe Fouquet said. AI demand pushed up the cost of certain types of chips as companies hoard semiconductors to power data centers, leading to a supply squeeze. Micron Technology Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra said last month that supplies of memory and storage chips would be much tighter in the coming years. In a bid to cash in on that tightness, ASML is seeking to increase production of its deep ultraviolet lithography tools as well as its more advanced extreme ultraviolet systems. In July, it had earmarked a 30% boost in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. However, Fouquet said it was becoming clear that wouldn't be enough to meet demand and that ASML was looking at ways to bolster capacity even more, especially for 2028 and beyond. Earlier this year, ASML executives alluded to the possibility of price increases, saying that a tight chip market gave ASML more negotiating power. Finance chief Roger Dassen said that while the company had now completed conversations with key customers, the effect of higher prices wouldn't show on 2026 figures. "It will start to become visible partly in the course of 2027. The full impact of that you will start to see in 2028 and beyond," he said. ASML posted sales of 11.66 billion euros for the third quarter, up from 7.52 billion euros a year earlier. historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries Gets $21 Billion for Plants in US-Japan Deal
historyItems.originalSummary: GlobalFoundries Inc plans to build two new chip plants with the backing of as much as US$21 billion from the Japanese government, part of an arrangement that also includes the US taking a 4 percent stake in the company. Under an agreement announced on Wednesday, GlobalFoundries will operate factories at its site in upstate New York that are jointly owned by the US and Japan. The facilities will be funded with money from Japan’s pledge to invest US$550 billion in the US. The factories will make so-called essential chips, the vital yet less sophisticated semiconductors used in vehicles, industrial equipment and communications gear. Photo: John Carl D’Annibale, The Albany Times Union via AP The GlobalFoundries agreement is meant to boost American production of essential chips and reduce dependence on East Asian suppliers — addressing a national security concern for the US. Under a broader arrangement with GlobalFoundries, the US Department of Commerce will take a roughly 4 percent equity stake in the company, “further enabling the American public to share in GF’s growth.” GlobalFoundries will get to redirect funds from a previous US CHIPS and Science Act grant to invest in honing its manufacturing abilities. That includes advancing its work in fields such as silicon photonics, chip packaging and silicon germanium. In a separate statement, the US Department of Commerce said it was reallocating US$955 million in CHIPS Act incentives to go toward GlobalFoundries’ factory expansion and modernization. As part of the agreement, the company will devote US$5 billion to capital investments at its plants in New York and Vermont. The new Japan-linked factories will be operated in the same way that GlobalFoundries runs its current facilities, which serve customers such as Apple Inc and Japanese firms including Renesas Electronics Corp. Profits will be divided among the owners and GlobalFoundries, following an approach laid out in last year’s US trade deal with Japan. US President Donald Trump touted the accord on his Truth Social site, saying it would help revitalize America’s industrial base and create jobs.

Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), Oracle and Super Micro also declined. Barclays analysts downgraded Dell, HPE and NetApp to the equivalent of hold from buy in a Wednesday report to clients. The analysts cited enterprise AI timing after significant stock gains. Barclays analysts said enterprise spending at Dell, HPE and NetApp had not shown a meaningful acceleration related to AI. The analysts instead attributed increased revenue to the global memory shortage. The analysts noted that infrastructure companies had passed higher memory prices on to customers. Barclays analysts said businesses typically allocate just 5% of IT budgets to AI, despite growing expectations that enterprise AI adoption will drive hardware replacement. The analysts found that only about a quarter of total enterprise AI spending goes toward hardware. The analysts said normalizing and eventually declining memory prices could weigh on infrastructure-related revenue. Data center server and other backend equipment makers have attracted investor interest this year on expectations of large equipment sales linked to AI demand for years ahead. Dell shares have risen more than 300% this year, making Dell one of the market's top performers. HPE shares have risen about 160% this year. NetApp shares have doubled this year. However, sentiment toward AI infrastructure has shifted recently, partly because of concerning revenue figures from OpenAI. Investors also fear that rising interest rates will create difficulties because much of the AI buildout relies on debt. Oracle, a heavy borrower, fell 9% on Wednesday and is now down 33% for the year. Neocloud company CoreWeave plunged 15% on Wednesday, erasing CoreWeave's gains for 2026. Memory is a highly cyclical business. Memory stocks fell this week after China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, also known as CXMT, reported progress over the weekend on a new chip structure. Micron shares are down 11% for the week. South Korea's SK Hynix has fallen 13% in U.S. trading this week. Western Digital has dropped more than 8% this week.

historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries to open 2 new chip plants in New York with $21 billion in financing from Japan
historyItems.originalSummary: MALTA, N.Y. — Computer chip company GlobalFoundries Inc. said Wednesday it plans to open two factories in Malta, New York, financed by an investment of up to US$21 billion from Japan. The company said the deal was made possible by the Trump administration’s trade and investment agreement with the Japanese government. It said the initiative will accelerate semiconductor manufacturing in the U.S. and strengthen critical supply chains. The company previously received some federal funding to expand as part of a Biden administration program to expand chip production. As a result of the investment from Japan, that federal funding will now go to investments in other areas to advance semiconductor manufacturing, GlobalFoundries spokesperson Kenneth Craig said in an email. U.S. President Donald Trump posted on social media that the U.S. government will receive shares in GlobalFoundries, just as it did for Intel Corp., in an expansion of the administration’s policy of taking ownership stakes in private companies. GlobalFoundries said in a statement that roughly US$10 billion would accelerate construction of a chip factory to open in 2029 and the other US$10 billion would fund a second plant. Demand for semiconductors has surged in recent years thanks to artificial intelligence and the need for computing power at data centers. In July, Taiwan computer chipmaker TSMC said it plans to spend another US$100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the U.S. TSMC has been expanding chip fabrication plants in the U.S., Japan and Taiwan.

historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries to Build Two Chip Plants With Up to $21 Billion Funding
historyItems.originalSummary: MALTA, N.Y. — Computer chip company GlobalFoundries Inc. said Wednesday it plans to open two factories in Malta, New York, financed by an investment of up to US$21 billion from Japan. The company said the deal was made possible by the Trump administration’s trade and investment agreement with the Japanese government. It said the initiative will accelerate semiconductor manufacturing in the U.S. and strengthen critical supply chains. The company previously received some federal funding to expand as part of a Biden administration program to expand chip production. As a result of the investment from Japan, that federal funding will now go to investments in other areas to advance semiconductor manufacturing, GlobalFoundries spokesperson Kenneth Craig said in an email. U.S. President Donald Trump posted on social media that the U.S. government will receive shares in GlobalFoundries, just as it did for Intel Corp., in an expansion of the administration’s policy of taking ownership stakes in private companies. GlobalFoundries said in a statement that roughly US$10 billion would accelerate construction of a chip factory to open in 2029 and the other US$10 billion would fund a second plant. Demand for semiconductors has surged in recent years thanks to artificial intelligence and the need for computing power at data centers. In July, Taiwan computer chipmaker TSMC said it plans to spend another US$100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the U.S. TSMC has been expanding chip fabrication plants in the U.S., Japan and Taiwan.

historyItems.originalTitle: Palantir and London mayor's office settle lawsuit over UK police contract
historyItems.originalSummary: In the United Kingdom, US technology company Palantir and the office of London Mayor Sadiq Khan have settled the company’s lawsuit over the decision not to approve a contract with London police worth £50 million, or $66 million. Channel NewsAsia reports , citing a joint statement by the parties. Palantir agreed with London police on a two-year contract to use artificial intelligence systems. They were intended to automate some tasks and help analyse evidence. However, London’s Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime refused to approve the agreement. It told police that no open competition had been held for the contract. Reports said that Khan’s representative also expressed concerns that Palantir did not align with London’s values. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . In a joint statement, Palantir and London’s Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime said they had settled the case and withdrawn their mutual allegations. The parties also said that the decision not to enter into the contract was not based on Palantir’s values or ethics, or on broader coverage of the company’s activities. The office said it does not and has never had a policy of refusing to enter into contracts with Palantir. The company may participate in future procurement procedures. The United Kingdom is also reviewing the National Health Service’s £330 million contract with Palantir. A parliamentary committee said there was a clear mismatch between the company and the United Kingdom’s values and recommended invoking an early termination clause. Louis Mosley, head of Palantir’s UK division, called the recommendation irresponsible.

historyItems.originalTitle: ASML's strong orders ease fears AI spending boom is running out of steam
historyItems.originalSummary: AMSTERDAM, Netherlands: Demand for advanced chipmaking equipment is stretching years into the future, with ASML saying customers are already looking to place orders for 2029 and even 2030 as the artificial intelligence investment boom continues to drive semiconductor expansion. The Dutch company, the world's biggest maker of equipment used to produce AI chips and advanced semiconductors, said October 14 that planned increases in its production capacity for 2027 and 2028 would not be enough to meet demand. ASML said in July that it planned to increase capacity by 30 percent in 2027 and by another 30 percent in 2028. CEO Christophe Fouquet said that the company was now seeing "a lot of order intake for 2028. But also, some strong interest to already place orders for 2029 and sometimes even 2030." The outlook helped ease investor concerns that the surge in spending on AI infrastructure could be approaching a peak. ASML's customers include TSMC, which manufactures chips for Nvidia, as well as Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix and Micron. The companies have been investing heavily to expand chip production. "There were concerns that the AI trade was running out of steam," said Gordon Kerr, European macro strategist at KBRA, adding ASML's results showed "demand for chips remains strong, and infrastructure spending is likely to continue well into 2027". ASML shares rose two percent on October 14. The stock has gained almost 70 percent this year, while the company is Europe's largest by market value at about €586 billion. The company reported third-quarter net profit of 4.96 billion euros on net sales of 11.7 billion euros. It forecast fourth-quarter sales of between 14.2 billion euros and 15.2 billion euros, or US$15.9 billion to $17 billion. ASML also raised its full-year sales outlook from at least 43 billion euros to 44 billion euros to 45 billion euros.

historyItems.originalSummary: Credo Launches Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Standardization for AI Data Center Scale-Up and Scale-Out Applications Joined by Initial Participants Including Leading Hyperscaler and Optical Technology Solution Providers AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC Under the OCP Networking Project Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (Credo) (NASDAQ: CRDO), an innovator in providing connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions, alongside prominent optical technology providers, today announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. Among the first to join with Credo include a leading hyperscaler as well as AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC, bringing together expertise spanning the full optical connectivity stack to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261012753816/en/ Credo, alongside prominent optical technology providers, has announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. Micro-emitter technology brings new ways of moving volumes of data, while dramatically improving reliability, power efficiency, and bandwidth density. Arrays of micron-scale light sources make up the transmit side of an optical link. Rather than pushing a few optical channels to extreme data rates, many micro-emitters operate in parallel at optimal individual speeds, enabling layer zero redundancy to improve reliability. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. The specification, targeted for OCP approval in 2027, will address requirements for link power, efficiency, signaling, parallelism, physical form factors – including module and connector footprint, link budget, and compliance. By defining specifications, the SRMO Workstream aims to give data center operators, hyperscalers, and system designers access to a broad ecosystem of interoperable components with supply chain resiliency, accelerating time to deployment and fostering continued innovation in optical connectivity. “As AI workloads scale from thousands to tens of thousands of accelerators, the industry needs a standardized approach to wide, parallel optical connectivity — not a patchwork of components that do not fit together or interoperate,” said L.K. historyItems.originalTitle: Department of Commerce Announces Agreement with GlobalFoundries to Amend Its Existing CHIPS Program Award and Reallocate $955 Million to Accelerate Investments in Silicon Photonics, Silicon-Germanium, and Advanced Packaging
historyItems.originalSummary: Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Program Office has agreed with GlobalFoundries to amend its existing award and reallocate up to $955 million in incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act. The amendment will increase the portion of an existing CHIPS Program award allocated to GlobalFoundries’ modernization and expansion of its semiconductor manufacturing facilities in Malta, NY and Burlington, VT. As part of the amendment, GlobalFoundries has agreed to expand its capital investment in these facilities to $5 billion. The total amount of the existing CHIPS Program award will not be increased. The investment will expand domestic manufacturing capacity for technologies increasingly critical to communications infrastructure and data centers, including silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and the first U.S.-based source of silicon interposers supporting advanced packaging technologies. “GlobalFoundries is expanding its investment to develop and manufacture critical semiconductor technologies enabling data center and high-performance compute infrastructure,” said Bill Frauenhofer, Executive Director for Semiconductor Innovation and Investment at the Department of Commerce. “The CHIPS Program award supports GlobalFoundries efforts to onshore and accelerate the development of these important semiconductor components." GlobalFoundries is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling technologies from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GlobalFoundries delivers differentiated, power efficient, and high-performance solutions for automotive, aerospace and defense, data center, smart mobile devices, internet of things and other high growth markets. historyItems.originalTitle: Oracle Proposes Plan that could deliver at least $155M to offset customers utility costs in New Mexico
historyItems.originalSummary: Austin, Texas-Oct 13, 2026 Oracle today announced a proposed Energy Service Agreement with El Paso Electric (EPE) for Project Jupiter to support late-stage construction, initial commissioning, emergency backup power at the site and to meet life safety needs for New Mexican workers at the data center. As indicated earlier this year, the primary power source for Project Jupiter will continue to be provided by the Bloom Energy fuel cell microgrid. There is no change to our plan. As part of the Energy Service Agreement, Oracle expects to pay $10 million for power annually for 10 years even if its usage is below contracted levels. This agreement helps offset shared electric system costs that would otherwise be borne by EPE's New Mexico customers and supports affordable electric rates. In addition, a separate agreement includes a proposal to provide as much as $55 million annually in direct credits for up to three years for EPE's New Mexico residential and small business customers. This credit could begin benefiting customers in 2027. "We welcome the opportunity to facilitate Oracle's credit to further affordability for our customers," said Kelly Tomblin, president and CEO of El Paso Electric. "Growth and investment in New Mexico has always been an EPE priority and we support the effort Oracle is making to ensure that this growth benefits our residential and small commercial customers." Earlier this year, Oracle signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge and made a commitment to pays its own way for energy and infrastructure costs. The proposed agreements with El Paso Electric not only ensure that Oracle pays for the energy costs, but it also supports affordable rates and additional offset of energy costs for its neighbors. "We realize the impact that electric rate increases have on the community and our proposed solution takes that burden off of New Mexico ratepayers," said Mahesh Thiagarajan, executive vice president, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. "We're taking this action now - well before our data center comes online - to deliver a direct, meaningful benefit to New Mexico households and small businesses and help ensure the community shares in the value created by Project Jupiter." Additional information will be provided following the filing of the Energy Service Agreement. historyItems.summary: NEW YORK, October 13. /TASS/. The US company SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying the Cargo Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday. The launch was streamed on the website of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Dragon Lifts Off for Thursday Cargo Delivery
historyItems.originalSummary: NEW YORK, October 13. /TASS/. The US company SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying the Cargo Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday. The launch was streamed on the website of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). The spacecraft lifted off from the spaceport at Cape Canaveral, Florida, at 06:33 a.m. local time (1:33 p.m. Moscow time/10:33 a.m. GMT) on the 35th resupply mission to the orbital station. Cargo Dragon will transport more than 2.8 tons of cargo to the orbiting outpost, including equipment for scientific experiments studying the effects of microgravity on heart tissue, as well as a set of solar arrays for the ISS. The spacecraft is expected to dock automatically with the ISS on October 15. In mid-November, Cargo Dragon is scheduled to return to Earth carrying the results of scientific experiments and equipment for repair.

historyItems.originalTitle: Credo Launches Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Standardization for AI Data Center Scale-Up and Scale-Out Applications - Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd
historyItems.originalSummary: Credo Launches Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Standardization for AI Data Center Scale-Up and Scale-Out Applications Joined by Initial Participants Including Leading Hyperscaler and Optical Technology Solution Providers AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC Under the OCP Networking Project Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (Credo) (NASDAQ: CRDO), an innovator in providing connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions, alongside prominent optical technology providers, today announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. Among the first to join with Credo include a leading hyperscaler as well as AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC, bringing together expertise spanning the full optical connectivity stack to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261012753816/en/ Credo, alongside prominent optical technology providers, has announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. Micro-emitter technology brings new ways of moving volumes of data, while dramatically improving reliability, power efficiency, and bandwidth density. Arrays of micron-scale light sources make up the transmit side of an optical link. Rather than pushing a few optical channels to extreme data rates, many micro-emitters operate in parallel at optimal individual speeds, enabling layer zero redundancy to improve reliability. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. The specification, targeted for OCP approval in 2027, will address requirements for link power, efficiency, signaling, parallelism, physical form factors – including module and connector footprint, link budget, and compliance. By defining specifications, the SRMO Workstream aims to give data center operators, hyperscalers, and system designers access to a broad ecosystem of interoperable components with supply chain resiliency, accelerating time to deployment and fostering continued innovation in optical connectivity. “As AI workloads scale from thousands to tens of thousands of accelerators, the industry needs a standardized approach to wide, parallel optical connectivity — not a patchwork of components that do not fit together or interoperate,” said L.K. historyItems.originalTitle: Celestica Introduces the DS6005 Data Center Switch with Co-Packaged Optics to Enable Power-Efficient AI Fabrics
historyItems.originalSummary: TORONTO, Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Celestica Inc. (NYSE: CLS) (TSX: CLS), a global leader in data center infrastructure and advanced technology solutions, today introduced the Celestica DS6005 , a co-packaged optics (CPO) data center switching system designed to address the bandwidth density, power, latency, and reach requirements of next-generation AI data center networks. Built on the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 – Davisson switch chip, the DS6005 is designed to deliver up to 102.4Tbps of switching capacity in a compact 1.5OU form factor designed for OCP ORv3 racks. By co-packaging optical engines with the switch ASIC, the DS6005 eliminates the need for traditional front-panel pluggable optics, helping data center operators optimize bandwidth density, reduce latency, and improve power efficiency in the AI data center. “AI infrastructure is driving unprecedented demand for bandwidth, while power, thermal management, latency, and reach are becoming increasingly important constraints,” said Gavin Cato, SVP & GM Portfolio Solutions & AI Platform Engineering, Celestica. “The DS6005 brings co-packaged optics, liquid cooling, field-replaceable external laser modules, and CPO-aware software management together in a compact platform designed to help customers build scalable and power-efficient AI fabrics.” Purpose-built to support AI/ML scale up and scale out networking, the DS6005 is a fully liquid-cooled, co-packaged optics data center switch that slashes power consumption and improves cluster efficiency while lowering latency and increasing reliability for next-generation AI clusters.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX stock poised for a catalyst-fueled 2027
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX ( SPCX ) isn't going quietly into what could be an eventful 2027. Elon Musk's rocket business said late last week it acquired a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio . It positions Musk's satellite business, Starlink, to challenge legacy wireless giants across the US. Shares of AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ), and Verizon ( VZ ) tanked on the news on Friday. Meanwhile, SpaceX is reportedly seeking to raise $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia chips. "The debate is whether a company this early in its public life should carry that much leverage," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said. historyItems.originalSummary: CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- As AI workloads drive demand for more scalable and flexible data center architectures, organizations are looking for faster, more efficient ways to move, store and protect data. Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) is helping to address these needs by expanding its portfolio of data center solutions with new innovations in PCIe ® connectivity, NVMe ® storage and acceleration that support high-performance computing infrastructure. "Customers are looking for technology partners that can address multiple challenges across the infrastructure stack while helping simplify design and accelerate deployment,” said Brian McCarson, corporate vice president and GM of Microchip’s data center solutions business unit. “By continuing to expand our portfolio, we're providing the building blocks needed to create more efficient, secure and adaptable platforms for today’s increasingly distributed and data-intensive computing environments.” Designed to bring PCIe Gen 6 connectivity to space- and power-constrained platforms, the Switchtec™ PCIe 6.0 Low-Lane-Count (LLC) switch provides up to 64 PCIe Gen 6 lanes, 32 ports and flexible x2, x4, x8 and x16 bifurcation options. Integrated Direct Memory Access (DMA) supports efficient peer-to-peer data movement between connected devices while reducing host CPU involvement. Like Microchip’s larger Switchtec Gen 6 devices, the LLC switch features PCIe Multicast and partitioning capabilities along with robust security through hardware root of trust and secure boot technologies. The new device delivers PCIe Gen 6 capabilities with a smaller, lower power footprint to extend support to a broader range of data center and intelligent edge applications. To address the industry’s requirements for secure, scalable and AI-optimized storage infrastructure, Microchip is updating its Flashtec ® SSD controller portfolio with an enhanced version of the PCIe Gen 5 NVMe 5016 controller. Building on the controller's high-performance, power-optimized architecture, the updated device adds support for Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite (CNSA) 2.0 to help customers prepare for emerging post-quantum security requirements. Dual-port capability enables highly available storage architectures through redundant data paths and load balancing, while advanced virtualization, Quality of Service (QoS) management and flexible programmability help optimize performance. Together, these enhancements extend the Flashtec platform’s ability to address evolving NAND technologies, high-capacity SSD designs and next-generation enterprise, hyperscale and AI deployments. Microchip is also expanding the capabilities of its Adaptec ® SmartRAID 4300 family of NVMe RAID storage accelerators with a series of enhancements designed to address practical operational needs. The updates are focused on strengthening storage security, minimizing downtime, expanding data protection and simplifying deployment across a wider range of environments. historyItems.originalTitle: Nokia to start dealing out GPUs in high-stakes AI-RAN gamble
historyItems.originalSummary: Some drivers are happy to run a car until the chassis has corroded and the engine coughs with every agonizing change of gear. Others less constrained by economic circumstances want a new vehicle every time the paint is nicked. Many big telcos currently seem to have more in common with the first group, determined to run their mobile networks until the basestations are shrouded in cobwebs. Any upgrades, including to 6G, should not have to require hardware replacement, they are telling vendors. Yet Nokia wants to sell them a completely new engine. The Finnish company has publicly teamed up with Nvidia to design radio access network (RAN) products built on the giant chipmaker's graphics processing units (GPUs). It has stopped developing new custom silicon with partner Marvell Technology, although it will continue to support its existing 4G and 5G range for years. Ultimately, however, customers will have to buy new hardware to enjoy new features. There is no guarantee the situation will be all that different for customers of Ericsson. Operators using its purpose-built 5G products today may need to invest in newer application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) to support forthcoming 5G-Advanced and 6G software. But Nokia's GPU strategy is undoubtedly much riskier. While commonplace in data centers and certain gadgets, Nvidia's chips have never been used for RAN compute. If telcos balk at the idea, Nokia could be in trouble. "If you don't have a companion strategy that's based on classic ASICs, you really have created jeopardy, I think," said Marcus Weldon, a former Nokia chief technology officer who was also president of its Bell Labs research unit. Yet the rewards could be immense if Nokia can prove that GPUs have advantages over ASICs in the RAN. In recent months, it has argued that its GPU-led strategy will support a doubling in spectral efficiency, among other benefits, by 2028. In a RAN market that is not expected to grow in the next few years, such improvements could justify the initial hardware outlay and even translate into market share gains for Nokia, allowing it to recover 5G ground lost to Ericsson and Samsung. That could be a disaster for Nokia's rivals. Numerous operators are now giving Nokia's AI-RAN products a test drive before they become commercially available early next year. None has yet said anything in public about the initial experience, and many operators have previously voiced concern about using what is still perceived to be a very expensive and energy-hungry chip in the RAN. Overkill has been the word on some lips, as if putting a GPU in the RAN is like using a rocket launcher to kill a rat. But Nokia has been advertising a slimline GPU that could be slotted into an existing Airscale chassis originally designed to support Marvell Technology's silicon. It will have to function with the same power constraints and be available for the same price, according to executives. They have also promised it will support software upgrades and new AI algorithms for years – unlike any ASIC. historyItems.originalTitle: Intel and Applied Materials Just Deepened Their AI Partnership. Which Stock Looks Better Positioned?
historyItems.originalSummary: Applied Materials Inc. (NASDAQ: AMAT ) and Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: INTC ) announced on October 6 that they are expanding their partnership on next-generation AI chipmaking. The two will work together on transistors, the wiring that connects them, and advanced packaging. That includes Intel's Foveros technology for stacking chips in 3D. Teams will work out of Applied's EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel's research campus in Oregon. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the goal is to move new technology from the lab into high-volume U.S. production faster. The Intel deal adds another dimension to Applied Materials' growth story. But before judging AMAT by its valuation, see what Jim Cramer thinks investors may be missing .

historyItems.summary: FormFactor (FORM) has been dropped from the S&P 600 and added to the S&P 400, a reshuffle that shifts the semiconductor tester into the mid cap index universe. The reshuffle lands on a stock that has already been very active, with FormFactor's 1 month share price return of 22.32% and year to date share price return of 135.97% pointing to strong momentum even after a 6.36% drop over the past week. At a latest share price of $139.67, that move sits on top of a 1 year total shareholder return of 266.20%. This builds on multi year total shareholder returns above 280% and indicates that investors have been steadily marking up both growth potential and risk appetite around the stock.

historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk's SpaceX just made a huge play to challenge the phone industry and stocks like AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are getting crushed
historyItems.originalSummary: Elon Musk’s SpaceX is moving past satellite internet, and it’s making a big move into the US wireless market. The company has agreed to buy cellular spectrum licences from investment firm Grain Management in a deal reportedly worth about $8 billion, its biggest move yet to compete with established mobile carriers such as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, according to a WSJ report . The deal is for spectrum in the 800MHz band, which is for mobile services delivered via terrestrial infrastructure such as cell towers, not satellites. If the acquisition is approved, SpaceX could combine those airwaves with its growing Starlink satellite network to create a more comprehensive wireless service. SpaceX has already been rolling out Starlink in areas beyond the usual broadband. The company has been working with T-Mobile for over a year to offer basic wireless connectivity in remote areas. SpaceX is also launching newer Starlink satellites that are capable of carrying more data. The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch up to 15,000 satellites dedicated to mobile services. Leaders at OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI companies are reportedly preparing for a potential AI disaster that could turn the public against artificial intelligence. According to an Axios report, industry leaders are privately running through possible scenarios for what happens after a catastrophic AI incident. What kind of AI disaster are companies preparing for? AI is a useful tool for handling many tasks in private as well as professional settings, but medical advice, especially diagnosis, is one area where I generally draw the line. General-purpose chatbots tend to sound confident and convincing while giving medical advice, even when they are wrong, as studies have previously found. That being said, Google's new research points to a much more convincing use for AI in healthcare. Its Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer chatbot, or AMIE for short, could help prepare both sides before the appointment even begins.

historyItems.title: TELUS 整合進度導致 AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) 估值可能被低估 67%
historyItems.summary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) moved back into focus after the company and TELUS completed their first integration test connecting TELUS' terrestrial wireless network with AST SpaceMobile's satellite based system for direct smartphone to satellite service in Canada. AST SpaceMobile's integration progress with TELUS comes after a volatile run for the stock, with the share price falling 6.13% over the past day and 13.90% over the past month, contributing to a 31.80% decline in the year to date. Long term total shareholder return over three and five years remains very large compared with the initial listing period, suggesting recent weakness reflects shifting risk expectations rather than a simple reversal of the broader multi year move.

historyItems.originalTitle: NASA Sets Coverage for SpaceX 35th Station Resupply Launch, Arrival
historyItems.originalSummary: A SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft departs from the International Space Station on June 16 after undocking from the Harmony module's forward port. Dragon, packed with completed science experiments and cargo for retrieval and analysis on Earth, parachuted to a splashdown off the coast of southern California the following day.NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT, Tuesday, Oct. 13, for the next launch to deliver science investigations, supplies, and equipment, including the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays, to the space station. This is the 35th SpaceX commercial resupply services mission to the orbital complex for NASA.NASA also will host a media teleconference on Thursday, Oct. 8 that will preview the cargo resupply flight, as well as provide a post-splashdown update for the agency's SpaceX Crew-12 mission, which will have returned to Earth from the space station Thursday morning.Loaded with more than 6,300 pounds of supplies, a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft on a Falcon 9 rocket will lift off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Dragon will dock autonomously around 11 a.m. on Thursday, Oct. 15, to the space-facing port of the station's Harmony module.NASA's live launch and docking coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online:https://www.nasa.gov/liveIn addition to the solar arrays, the Dragon spacecraft will deliver hardware to manufacture artificial retinas in microgravity to help restore vision on Earth and 3D heart tissues models to advance large-scale drug testing on future missions. The spacecraft will carry materials to study how a new type of glass forms in microgravity and brain organoids that could reveal treatment targets for neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and multiple sclerosis.The Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the space station until mid-November when it will depart the orbiting laboratory and return to Earth with time-critical research and cargo, splashing down off the coast of California.NASA's mission coverage is as follows (all times Eastern and subject to change based on real-time operations):Thursday, Oct. 81:15 p.m.: International Space Station briefing for Crew-12 return, and SpaceX's 35th Commercial Resupply Services launch with the following participants:Bill Spetch, deputy manager of Commercial, Low Earth Orbit ProgramDr. Liz Warren, deputy chief scientist, NASA's International Space Station OfficeLee Echerd, senior mission manager, Customer Operations and Integration, SpaceXAndreas Mogensen, leader, Human Exploration Group, ESA (European Space Agency)To participate in the teleconference, media must contact the NASA Johnson Space Center newsroom for call details by 12 p.m., Oct. 8, at: jsccommu@mail.nasa.gov or 281-483-5111. To ask questions, media must dial in no later than 10 minutes before the start of the call. historyItems.originalTitle: Judge could order Nebius to halt data center construction in Independence
historyItems.originalSummary: A motions hearing is set for Oct. 22 on a lawsuit related to the Nebius data center project in Independence.The Independence GUARD (Guardians United Against Reckless Development) Alliance filed the lawsuit to halt construction of the Nebius hyperscale AI data factory in the Little Blue Valley.Named in the lawsuit are the city of Independence, Missouri ADC Holdings LLC (data center developer) and Independence Power Partners LP.Residents along Bly Road in the Little Blue Valley are hoping to stop construction near their homes.The lawsuit alleges the city violated zoning and sunshine laws, as well as the city charter, and has failed to enforce city laws. Residents are asking a judge to pause the project.A hearing has been set for 9 a.m. on Oct. 22 on their motion for a temporary restraining order and the defendants' motion to dismiss.The Independence City Council approved billions of dollars in incentives for Dutch tech company Nebius to build and operate the 2.1-million-square-foot hyperscale AI data factory on 400 acres at the south end of Bly Road in March. Nebius broke ground on the first phase of the project in April.Nebius — which is party to the lawsuit through a subsidiary, Missouri ADC Holdings — provided us a statement about the lawsuit when it was filed earlier this year in Jackson County Circuit Court.“We are reviewing the claims and cannot comment on the case specifics,” Nebius Vice President of Public Affairs John Sutter said in a statement. “Nebius remains committed to complying with all applicable laws and regulations, and being a responsible partner for the community as our historic investment in Independence takes shape.”—

Traditional burn-in holds devices in banks of dedicated ovens at a controlled air temperature for hours before they move on to functional test.Teradyne Titan HP instead holds each device at its target junction temperature while running a realistic device workload, so reliability stress functions are optimized and thermal controls are enabled at the per-device level.
historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne enhances Titan HP for AI chip reliability tests
historyItems.originalSummary: Teradyne, Inc. announced a production-ready system that delivers enhanced burn-in capabilities on its Titan? HP platform. Traditional burn-in holds devices in banks of dedicated ovens at a controlled air temperature for hours before they move on to functional test.Teradyne Titan HP instead holds each device at its target junction temperature while running a realistic device workload, so reliability stress functions are optimized and thermal controls are enabled at the per-device level. Titan HP can be used for system level test or reliability testing, optimizing capital cost investments. For reliability testing, every device carries its full stress-and-test history on a single record.Per-site thermal control, tuned to each device's thermal and force zones, and paired with high per-device kilowatt power delivery, lets Titan HP sustain reliability-stress conditions on parts whose power draw and heat dissipation strain a conventional oven flow. The platform's asynchronous slot architecture loads and tests each slot independently, so a long stress run on one device does not idle the rest of the system, and individual sites can be serviced while the system continues to operate. Test programs run on the Teradyne Atlas software platform, which lets engineers import existing programs or build new ones and port them to other Teradyne system level test systems. Burn-in has long been standard for automotive and other high-reliability silicon.AI accelerators and cloud infrastructure devices are now entering the same category, driven by the high cost of a single failed accelerator in a deployed rack. Enhanced burn-in extends Teradyne?s test portfolio, which spans the AI device supply chain from wafer to data center.
